fields.name: value
fields.documentation: A response tuning curve. The stimulus dimensions it is tabulated over (direction, contrast, spatial/temporal frequency, ...) are the value's `dimensions` -- one each, with the levels as a covariate along it (categorical levels as `term`), when the conditions tested form a full grid over those variables; otherwise ONE `stimulus condition` dimension, one position per condition tested, with a covariate per variable along it (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [tuning grid], V_eta_data_body_model_plan.md; the `stimulus condition` dimension is XCO:0000000 experimental condition, [stimulus condition term]) -- so which family a curve belongs to is its covariates' `variable`s, not a subclass. Statistics of the response are separate named fields (T14: another reading of the same quantity is a position along a dimension, a different statistic of it is its own field). On a calculation the value also holds the fits (`model_fit`) and, beside them, their `significance` (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [one fit entry], [significance with results]); an observed curve leaves both empty. (#73 audit 2 D3: `independent_variables[]` dropped -- it restated the keys, now `dimensions` + `covariates`.)

fields.name: mean
fields.documentation: Per-sample mean response, sized by the value's `dimensions` (the stimulus dimensions).

fields.name: stddev
fields.documentation: Per-sample response standard deviation, sized by the value's `dimensions` (the stimulus dimensions).

fields.name: stderr
fields.documentation: Per-sample response standard error of the mean, sized by the value's `dimensions` (the stimulus dimensions).

fields.name: individual
fields.documentation: Per-trial individual response values: the value's `dimensions` plus ONE trailing trial dimension. When the response is complex (`response_type` F1 or F2), one more trailing component dimension of size 2 follows the trial dimension: [real, imaginary], so both parts of NDI's complex response are kept. `mean`/`stddev`/`stderr` are unchanged: NDI computes them from the complex trials, and `mean` is the magnitude (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21 [complex trial responses]). Responses may be normalized or control-subtracted.

fields.name: raw_individual
fields.documentation: OPTIONAL: unprocessed per-trial responses BEFORE control subtraction or normalization; the value's `dimensions` plus ONE trailing trial dimension. When the response is complex (`response_type` F1 or F2), one more trailing component dimension of size 2 follows the trial dimension: [real, imaginary], so both parts of NDI's complex response are kept. `mean`/`stddev`/`stderr` are unchanged: NDI computes them from the complex trials, and `mean` is the magnitude (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21 [complex trial responses]).

fields.name: control
fields.documentation: The control/blank response block (nested for symmetry with the response statistics; avoids parallel `control_*` prefixed fields).

fields.name: mean
fields.documentation: Mean response to the control/blank stimulus.

fields.name: stddev
fields.documentation: Standard deviation of the control response.

fields.name: stderr
fields.documentation: Standard error of the mean of the control response.

fields.name: individual
fields.documentation: Per-trial individual control response values; ONE trial dimension. When the response is complex (`response_type` F1 or F2), one more trailing component dimension of size 2 follows the trial dimension: [real, imaginary], so both parts of NDI's complex response are kept. `mean`/`stddev`/`stderr` are unchanged: NDI computes them from the complex trials, and `mean` is the magnitude (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21 [complex trial responses]).

fields.name: pooled
fields.documentation: Optional: the standard deviation and standard error of the blank-trial responses pooled over trials, computed by NDIcalc-vis spatial/temporal frequency tuning from the first stimulus's control trials taken as magnitudes (v1 control_mean_stddev / control_mean_stderr). Distinct from control.stddev/stderr, which are per stimulus (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21 [pooled blank statistics]).

fields.name: stddev
fields.documentation: Optional: the standard deviation of the blank-trial responses pooled over trials (v1 control_mean_stddev).

fields.name: stderr
fields.documentation: Optional: the standard error of the blank-trial responses pooled over trials (v1 control_mean_stderr).

fields.name: response_unit
fields.documentation: The unit of the response arrays (e.g. hertz for a spike rate; what is measured, such as firing rate, goes in the statement's `variable`: Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [response variable]), a registered unit term, bound (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [remaining units bound]).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: response_type
fields.documentation: The reduction applied to each stimulus presentation to yield a per-trial response: mean | peak | F0 | F1 | F2 (#73 audit 2 D3; replaces free text and contrast's `modulated_response` flag, which said F1 vs F0).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: coordinates
fields.documentation: The coordinate basis for angle-valued independent variables (e.g., 'compass', 'cartesian'). Absent for non-angular curves.

fields.name: model_fit
fields.documentation: ARRAY of fitted models, set only on a calculation (`tuning_curve_calculation` and its named calculators; an observed curve leaves it empty). Each entry is THE fit entry (model_fit.value's shape, Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [one fit entry]) with the values read off it (`metrics`) beside it; a curve may carry several co-existing fits (frequency tunings carry 5).

fields.name: model
fields.documentation: The fitted model, a term (naka_rushton, von_mises, double_gaussian, ...; a label when no term exists), bound (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [one fit entry]). <- v1 `fit_name`.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: equation
fields.documentation: The formula as written, evaluable against the coefficients' labels ("y=a+b*x.^c"). <- v1 `fit_equation`.

fields.name: independent_variables
fields.documentation: The fit's inputs, in `equation` order. <- v1 `fit_independent_variable_names`.

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: The variable, as a term or a label ({name}, no node).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: unit
fields.documentation: Canonical unit; absent for a categorical variable. Bound (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [remaining units bound]).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: dependent_variable
fields.documentation: The fit's output. <- v1 `fit_dependent_variable_names`.

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: The variable, as a term or a label ({name}, no node).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: unit
fields.documentation: Canonical unit; absent for a categorical variable. Bound (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [remaining units bound]).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: coefficients
fields.documentation: The fitted coefficients, one entry each, NAMED: `variable` is a term, or a label naming the coefficient (its symbol in the model's equation). (#73 audit 2 D2: one fit entry for every fit.) <- v1 `fit_parameters` zipped with `fit_parameter_names`.

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: Which coefficient: a term, or a label ({name}, no node).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Its value.

fields.name: constraints
fields.documentation: Constraints the fit was held to, one entry each. <- v1 `fit_constraints`.

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: Which coefficient: a term, or a label naming the symbol in `equation` ("a", "b", "c").

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Its value.

fields.name: goodness
fields.documentation: How well the fit matches the measured responses.

fields.name: r2
fields.documentation: Coefficient of determination between the responses and the fit (v1 `r2` / `r_squared`).

fields.name: sse
fields.documentation: Sum of squared errors of the fit.

fields.name: sse_per_point
fields.documentation: Sum of squared errors per fitted point (v1 vmspikefit `fit_sse_perpoint`).

fields.name: sampled_fit
fields.documentation: OPTIONAL: the fit evaluated on a grid, as v1 stored it. Kept rather than recomputed from model + coefficients, because recomputation reproduces it only if the model definition is exact.

fields.name: independent_values
fields.documentation: The grid: one entry per fit input, in the order of the fitted value's dimensions (a model_fit's `independent_variables`).

fields.name: response
fields.documentation: Fit response at each grid point, sized by the grid.

fields.name: input_field
fields.documentation: Field path, in the fitted document, of the independent values ("mydocumenttype.x"). <- v1 `fit_data.input_data_field`.

fields.name: output_field
fields.documentation: Field path, in the fitted document, of the dependent values. <- v1 `fit_data.output_data_field`.

fields.name: metrics
fields.documentation: The values read off THIS fit, beside the fit entry: the tuning calculator's own results (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [one fit entry]).

fields.name: preferred_value
fields.documentation: The independent-variable value at which the peak response occurs (v1 `pref`). Same unit as the curve's independent variable. In the unit of the curve's covariate along the tuned dimension (its `unit`), by rule `fit_metric_unit`; on a spatial-frequency curve cycles per degree, on a temporal-frequency curve hertz (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: half_maximum_below
fields.documentation: The independent-variable value BELOW the peak where the response falls to half the maximum (v1 `l50`; on a contrast curve, which only rises, this is C50 -- v1 `interpolated_c50`). -Inf if no such point exists. In the unit of the curve's covariate along the tuned dimension, by rule `fit_metric_unit`.

fields.name: half_maximum_above
fields.documentation: The independent-variable value ABOVE the peak where the response falls to half the maximum (v1 `h50`). +Inf if no such point exists. In the unit of the curve's covariate along the tuned dimension, by rule `fit_metric_unit`.

fields.name: bandwidth
fields.documentation: Bandwidth between half_maximum_below and half_maximum_above, in OCTAVES: log2(half_maximum_above / half_maximum_below). Inf if either bound is infinite. In the unit of the curve's covariate along the tuned dimension, by rule `fit_metric_unit`.

fields.name: half_width_at_half_maximum
fields.documentation: Angular distance from the preferred direction at which the fit response is half the maximum (v1 `hwhh`). Same unit as the curve's direction variable. In degrees, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: orientation_preference
fields.documentation: Orientation evoking the maximum response under the fit (v1 `orientation_angle_preference`). In degrees, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: direction_preference
fields.documentation: Direction evoking the maximum response under the fit (v1 `direction_angle_preference`). In degrees, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: orientation_preferred_orthogonal_ratio
fields.documentation: Fit response at the preferred orientation over the response at the orthogonal orientation (90 degrees away).

fields.name: orientation_preferred_orthogonal_ratio_rectified
fields.documentation: orientation_preferred_orthogonal_ratio with each response rectified at 0.

fields.name: direction_preferred_null_ratio
fields.documentation: Fit response at the preferred direction over the response at the null direction (180 degrees away).

fields.name: direction_preferred_null_ratio_rectified
fields.documentation: direction_preferred_null_ratio with each response rectified at 0.

fields.name: speed_tuning_index
fields.documentation: Index relating preferred speed to spatial frequency under the fit (Priebe et al.; v1 `priebe_fit_speed_tuning_index`).

fields.name: spatial_frequency_preference
fields.documentation: Spatial frequency, averaged across temporal frequencies, of the optimal response under the fit (v1 `priebe_fit_spatial_frequency_preference`). In cycles per degree, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: temporal_frequency_preference
fields.documentation: Temporal frequency, averaged across spatial frequencies, of the optimal response under the fit (v1 `priebe_fit_temporal_frequency_preference`). In hertz, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: partial_r2
fields.documentation: Partial r-squared of this fit against the nested comparison fit.

fields.name: nested_f_test_p
fields.documentation: p-value of the nested-model F test against the comparison fit (v1 `priebe_fit_nested_f_test_p_value`).

fields.name: significance
fields.documentation: Statistical significance of the tuning (ANOVA p-values), beside the fits (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [significance with results]). Set only on a calculation: computed by the fit calculator per paper sec. 2.1, not carried by the raw curve.

fields.name: visual_response_anova_p
fields.documentation: p-value of the ANOVA relating mean response values between the raw (stimulus) and control groups.

fields.name: across_stimuli_anova_p
fields.documentation: p-value of the ANOVA relating mean response values across different stimuli (tuning vs. flat).

rules.name: fit_metric_unit
rules.statement: A fit metric with no fixed unit (`preferred_value`, `half_maximum_below`, `half_maximum_above`, `bandwidth`) is in the `unit` of the curve's covariate along the tuned dimension; orientation and direction preferences and the half width at half maximum are degrees, a spatial-frequency preference cycles per degree and a temporal-frequency preference hertz (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).
